chunks: And ʿAlī ibn Jaʿfar asked his brother Mūsā ibn Jaʿfar عليهما السلام:

About the mukātab: is the fiṭrah of the month of Ramaḍān upon him, or upon the one who contracted his emancipation for him? And is his testimony admissible? He said: "The fiṭrah is upon him, and his testimony is not admissible."

key_terms.الْمُكَاتَبِ: a slave under a contractual arrangement to earn freedom
key_terms.شَهَادَتُهُ: his testimony in a legal or judicial context
key_terms.شَهْرِ رَمَضَانَ: the month of Ramaḍān, the fasting month
key_terms.فِطْرَةُ: zakat al-fitr, the alms due at the end of Ramaḍān
key_terms.كَاتَبَهُ: the person who made the emancipation contract with him

ai.seo_question: Is zakat al-fitr obligatory on a mukatab, and is his testimony accepted?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning the mukātab, a slave under a contract of emancipation. It states that zakat al-fitr is obligatory upon the mukātab himself, while his legal testimony is not accepted. The narration is significant in fiqh for rulings related to financial obligation and judicial capacity.
